newsitem.title: CHINA: China shrugs off Blair boycott of new HK MPs.
newsitem.headline: China shrugs off Blair boycott of new HK MPs.

text.p: China on Thursday shrugged off a plan by British Prime Minister Tony Blair to boycott a ceremony to swear in Hong Kong's post-handover legislature.

Blair said on Wednesday he would attend a ceremony to mark the handover of Hong Kong to China at midnight on June 30, but would leave before the swearing-in ceremony of the non-elected provisional legislature that will replace Hong Kong's democratically elected parliament.
"It is estimated that 4,000 people have been invited to attend this ceremony," Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman Cui Tiankai told a news briefing.
"If there are individuals who for whatever reasons cannot attend, it will not affect the ceremony from being held smoothly," he said.
Cui defended the non-elected legislature, saying it was an inseparable part of the post-handover government.
The spokesman said China welcomed Blair's attendance at the handover ceremony.

The West has criticised Beijing for replacing the current parliament with the provisional legislature, whose 400 members were hand-picked by China in a move that effectively scrapped the colony's democratic reforms.
The United States said on Tuesday that Secretary of State Madeleine Albright would boycott the investiture of the non-elected legislature.
It remained to be seen whether Britain's other main partners, some of which have signed major trade deals with China, would follow suit.
Britain has been arguing for months with China over details of the handover ceremony but concedes it can do little to prevent the new legislature being sworn in.
China takes over Hong Kong at midnight on June 30 after 156 years of colonial rule.
